key_insight: NPC-RubricBench evaluates how well large language models reason across a patient's cancer care journey, rather than at a single clinical visit. It uses patient-specific, phase-aware rubrics in nasopharyngeal carcinoma care.
problem_solved: Most medical LLM evaluations focus on isolated encounters, missing how clinical responsibilities and patient needs change throughout longitudinal cancer care.
method: Introduce a benchmark grounded in longitudinal records from 405 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
Use patient-specific rubrics to assess reasoning in the context of individual care trajectories.
Evaluate multistage clinical reasoning with criteria that reflect changing responsibilities across care phases.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this benchmark offers a way to assess clinical reasoning beyond single-visit accuracy. The supplied abstract is truncated, so model comparisons and performance findings are not available.
visual_elements: Patient care timeline showing evolving clinical responsibilities across phases.
Rubric grid mapping care phases to patient-specific evaluation criteria.
Side-by-side illustration contrasting single-encounter testing with longitudinal evaluation.
Dataset icon highlighting longitudinal records from 405 patients.
paper_title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
paper_authors: Wei-Wei Zhang, Pengkai Wang, Yan Li, Zhijie Sang, Guan-Qun Zhou
